title: Prime cyclic coefficient is a retract of a nonzero ring quotient
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $h:Y\to X$ a morphism of schemes, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $r$ a prime natural number which is not a unit in $\Lambda$ [def-pc-scheme]. Write $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$ and use the constant module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If $R^qh_*\underline{\Lambda/(r)}=0$, then $R^qh_*\underline{P_r/(r)}=0$, with higher direct images computed in the corresponding module-sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Tag 0F08 (proof, cyclic-coefficient reduction); Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree); Tag 0739 (lemma-colimit), with the arbitrary-ring coefficient argument explicitly supplied here

proof.text: If $1\in(r)$, an expression $1=ar$ makes $r$ a unit. Therefore $V=\Lambda/(r)$ is nonzero. Since $r$ is prime, $V$ is an $\mathbf F_r$-vector space and its vector $1$ is nonzero. Mathlib Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one over the field $\mathbf F_r$ supplies a linear functional $\phi:V\to\mathbf F_r$ with $\phi(1)=1$. The inclusion $a\mapsto a\cdot1$ and $\phi$ give an additive retraction.

Apply the constant abelian sheaf functor and then abelian $R^qh_*$ to the retraction identities. Thus the degree-$q$ image for $\mathbf F_r$ is a retract of the degree-$q$ image for $V$. A retract of zero is zero: its identity factors through the zero object and is therefore zero.

By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying], the two constant module sheaves have underlying abelian sheaves $V$ and $\mathbf F_r$. Resolve them by injective module sheaves. Their underlying abelian sheaves are direct-image acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-module-direct-image-acyclic], so the same pushforward complexes compute their underlying abelian higher direct images. Forgetting coefficients is faithful and exact, and hence reflects zero objects. Together with the fact that $(r)=0$ in $P_r$, the abelian vanishing from the previous step is exactly the desired module-sheaf vanishing. For negative degrees both sides vanish; degree zero is ordinary pushforward.
